explanation: For motion with constant acceleration the position is x(t) = x0 + v0*t + 1/2 a*t^2 and the velocity is v(t) = v0 + a*t. The position function is a parabola in time whose curvature is set by a, while v0 is the initial slope; a velocity arrow on the particle shows v reversing sign when v0 and a have opposite signs. This is one of the core AP kinematics equations and shows up in nearly every mechanics problem. The dot rides a real track with numbered position ticks and the readout reports x and v at each instant.
bullets: Position is a parabola in t; its curvature is set by acceleration a.
Velocity arrow = v0 + a*t; it can reverse when a opposes v0.
x0 = 0 here, so x is the displacement from the start.
Track ticks are real meters; the dot's x matches the lower graph.
